title: Copilot Can Find What People Can Access
description: Looking at SharePoint permissions, oversharing and Microsoft Copilot.
series: Who’s in Control When Everyone Can Build a Copilot?
bodyHtml:
When we talk about Copilot governance, we often talk about policies, agents and what users should be allowed to do. But what about the data users already have access to?

For example, someone in your organisation has access to a SharePoint site from a project that ended two years ago. Nobody has reviewed the permissions since.

That person might not even remember having access to the site. But when asking Copilot a question, information from that site could become part of the answer.

Copilot hasn't given that person any additional permissions. The permissions were already there.

Where do you start?

One of the things you can look at is the Data Access Governance reports in the SharePoint admin center.

Go to Reports > Data access governance.

These reports can help you find sites with broad permissions and files that have been shared more widely than intended.

You can use this information to work with site owners and review who still needs access.

What if you need more time?

There are two options in SharePoint Advanced Management that I wanted to take a closer look at.

Restricted Content Discovery

You can use this setting to prevent content from a specific SharePoint site from appearing in organisation-wide search and Copilot discovery experiences.

People can still access the site directly if they have permission.

This could be useful if you have several SharePoint sites where permissions still need to be reviewed.

Restricted Access Control

With this setting, you can restrict access to a SharePoint site to specific Microsoft 365 or Entra security groups.

Even if someone previously had access to a document, they also need to be a member of one of the configured groups.

There is an important difference between these two settings. The first restricts how content can be found. The second restricts access to the content itself.

Both require the appropriate licensing.

What about Copilot Studio?

Things can get a bit more complicated when building agents in Copilot Studio.

For example, when an agent uses a Power Automate flow to retrieve information from SharePoint, whose connection is being used? Is it the connection of the user or a connection configured by the maker?

Depending on how this is set up, the agent could have access to information that the user normally cannot access.

Something to check when reviewing an agent before publishing it.

Where to go from here

You don't have to wait until Copilot is introduced to start reviewing your SharePoint permissions.

Start with a few sites that contain sensitive information. Check who has access, how documents are shared and whether the site still has an active owner.

I think this is also something worth including in a regular governance review. Permissions change, people leave the company and new SharePoint sites are created all the time.
